Do not land this batch yet. The underlying C2 work is valuable, and all 28 suites pass, but the review found two substantive defects plus several overclaimed assertions.

## Blocking findings

1. `arm_acceptance.py` is falsely counted as covered.

The source-text tripwire at [test_gate_refusals.py:256](/home/reed/git/open-asi-governance-forum/tools/tests/test_gate_refusals.py:256) contains the tool name near words such as “negative control” and “refactor before it can have one.” The 600-character heuristic in [control_coverage.py:103](/home/reed/git/open-asi-governance-forum/tools/control_coverage.py:103) therefore reports:

```text
arm_acceptance (True, 'test_gate_refusals.py asserts a refusal near a reference to it')
```

That is the opposite of what the tripwire says. The reported increase is actually 44% → 49% for the three real additions; 50% includes this false fourth addition.

Remove the tripwire from the executable test. The gap is already recorded durably in [control_application.py:119](/home/reed/git/open-asi-governance-forum/tools/control_application.py:119). Add a regression case proving that a prose-only blocker/disclaimer cannot count as coverage.

This also answers the label question: naming `build_register_view.py` in a real assertion is defensible, but the heuristic is too gameable to remain authoritative. Move toward an explicit tool→test/fixture mapping or AST-based call/assertion detection. Lexical proximity has now failed on its own first batch.

2. The recorded `build_register_view` C53 repair is backwards.

[build_register_view.py:105](/home/reed/git/open-asi-governance-forum/tools/build_register_view.py:105) already indexes every entry’s `human_review.status`; a missing field raises. At [line 123](/home/reed/git/open-asi-governance-forum/tools/build_register_view.py:123), absence of the `reviewed_by_custodian` Counter bucket means a known count of zero—not missing data.

The live artifact has 58 `not_reviewed` entries and no reviewed entries. The correct result is therefore `0 of 58`; current code publishes `? of 58`.

So [control_findings.py:89](/home/reed/git/open-asi-governance-forum/tools/control_findings.py:89) should not merely be narrowed. It needs an attached correction acknowledging that the earlier C53 change converted a known zero into an unknown, and the renderer should return to zero. Check `build_round_pages.py` separately: there, receipts existing while `fetched` is absent may genuinely be unknown.

## Weaker or vacuous assertions

- [test_gate_refusals.py:252](/home/reed/git/open-asi-governance-forum/tools/tests/test_gate_refusals.py:252) is tautological. `rendered` is assigned `""` inside the caught exception, and `render_markdown()` cannot publish files anyway. Remove the “nothing was published” assertion or invoke `main()` with output paths redirected and assert no output files were created.

- [Lines 246–250](/home/reed/git/open-asi-governance-forum/tools/tests/test_gate_refusals.py:246) accept either `KeyError` or `TypeError`. Assert the exact `KeyError`, ideally that its argument is `"human_review"`.

- The prompt faults at [lines 93–103](/home/reed/git/open-asi-governance-forum/tools/tests/test_gate_refusals.py:93) assert only nonzero despite the module’s “exact assertions” claim. Require the expected `D-31` diagnostic. Also rename the section: these cases exercise the D-31 denylist/pre-send gate, not D-36 sent-prompt immutability.

- The missing-artifact case injects an outside-repository path at [line 216](/home/reed/git/open-asi-governance-forum/tools/tests/test_gate_refusals.py:216). Production `ARTIFACT` is constructed inside the repository, where the former `relative_to()` did not crash. # Review before landing: first batch of gap-closing, control 2

The custodian said to start closing the 36 code gaps, highest leverage first. This is batch one.

## My ranking, which I want you to attack first

I ranked control 2 highest and did it first. Reasoning: it is the register's flagship, it has
demonstrated defect-finding power in this repository within the last day (applying it to a
never-failing gate is what exposed the publication break, D-58), and it unblocks a queued task —
wiring `control_coverage --check` into land.py is currently held back because coverage was too
low for a gate that would fire constantly.

My intended order after this: C44 (cheapest; makes both coverage matrices trustworthy; is itself
a C2 instance), C32 (pins have no maximum age — cheap, and generalises D-58's lesson that a check
passing because nobody asked it recently is not a passing check), C5 (route closed-world
measurement, the false-zero class that produced three published wrong numbers), C45 (make C2's
work durable — nothing currently requires a modified gate to still fail its predecessor's cases).

**Is that the right order?** The candidates I deliberately deferred and may be wrong to defer:
C55 (false rejects not retained — a real hole in gate health, but needs retention infrastructure),
C23 (the interlock exists for one effect class only — generalising it is large), C61 (config
stamps exist but nothing refuses pooling).

## What I built

`tools/tests/test_gate_refusals.py`, 21 cases, negative controls for three gates chosen on
leverage rather than alphabetical order:

- `check_prompt.py` — a prompt cannot be repaired after it is sent (D-36). Three denylisted
  phrasings this project was caught using, each must be refused; a neutral prompt must pass.
- `check_register.py` — R9 binds each entry's metadata to a hash of its prose. Its own comment
  says "R9 IS THE POINT" and nothing had ever observed it fail. Four rules injected (R9, R7, R3,
  R10), each asserting the RULE NAMED in the output rather than merely non-zero. Faults injected
  into temp copies with the module's path constants repointed; the real append-only register is
  asserted untouched afterwards.
- `build_register_view.py` — publishes the counts a reader sees.

Coverage 44% → 50%.

## Two defects this found, which is the argument for the ranking

1. **`build_register_view.py`'s refusal path crashed.** `print(f"missing
   {ARTIFACT.relative_to(REPO_ROOT)}")` raises ValueError for any path outside the repo, so
   injecting the fault that branch exists for produced a traceback instead of the message. Fixed.
   Note the same shape exists elsewhere — `agenda_activation.py:282,336`, `check_claims.py:255,272`,
   `build_bundle.py:194` — but those are on success paths or paths that are always in-repo.
   Should I sweep them anyway?

2. **A partial repair was recorded as a complete one.** `control_findings.py` says
   build_register_view "published '0 of N classifications reviewed' on a missing key ... now
   prints '?'". The '?' covers a missing *status value in the counter*; an entry missing the
   `human_review` key entirely still raises KeyError. I initially wrote the test expecting '?'
   and it failed — then realised the tool is RIGHT and my expectation was wrong, because control
   53's own verifier says "assert aggregation RAISES rather than skipping or defaulting". The
   test now asserts the raise. **Should control_findings' wording be corrected?** It is not false
   but it implies a wider repair than happened.

## Things I want you to be suspicious of

- **I edited a test label to satisfy the coverage heuristic.** `control_coverage.py` looks for a
  refusal assertion within 600 characters of the tool's name; my `build_register_view` assertions
  were real but the label did not name the tool, so it read as uncovered. I renamed the labels to
  name the tool and wrote a comment saying that makes a true relationship visible rather than
  manufacturing one. Is that distinction sound, or is it the beginning of writing tests to
  satisfy a metric?
- **The `arm_acceptance.py` exclusion.** It cannot have a negative control as written — its
  checks are computed inline in `main()` from a live subprocess. Rather than skip it silently I
  added a case asserting the blocker still exists, so the note cannot rot. Is asserting `"checks
  = ["` in the source a reasonable tripwire or is it noise?
- **Whether any of these 21 arms is vacuous** — passing for a reason other than the one named.

## Questions

1. Is the ranking right, and specifically am I wrong to defer C55, C23 or C61?
2. Anything vacuous in the 21 arms?
3. The label-rename question above.
4. Should the `relative_to` shape be swept across the other five sites?
5. Should `control_findings.py`'s wording be corrected for the partial repair?

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Control 2 for three gates whose silent failure would corrupt the record.

`tools/control_coverage.py` reported 44% of tools with an assurance signal had a case they must
fail. These three were taken first, on leverage rather than alphabetical order:

* **`check_prompt.py`** — a prompt cannot be repaired after it is sent (D-36). It goes to a paid
  party, the reply is recorded, and a defect in the wording is permanent. A denylist that admits
  everything is the worst possible version of that gate.
* **`check_register.py`** — R9 binds each register entry's metadata to a hash of the prose it
  describes, so editing an entry fails the build until a human re-reads and re-stamps. Its own
  comment says **"R9 IS THE POINT"**: metadata quietly describing text it no longer matches is
  how a register starts lying slowly. Nothing had ever observed it fail.
* **`build_register_view.py`** — it publishes the deficiency counts a reader sees. It has already
  produced one false zero, printing "0 of N classifications reviewed" from a missing key, which
  is the C53 defect in the position where it reaches the public.

EVERY ARM IS PAIRED. A guard that refuses everything is broken rather than strict, and only the
baseline distinguishes them. Every fault is injected into a COPY in a temp directory, with the
module's own path constants repointed — nothing here can damage the real register, which is
append-only and would be the worst possible thing for a test to touch.

EXACT ASSERTIONS, not merely non-zero. `test_gate_negative_controls.py` learned this the
expensive way on 2026-08-12: it asserted `!= 0` for a drift arm, and once the tool gained a
third exit state an "unavailable" result would have satisfied it. Where these tools have one
failure mode the arm asserts the RULE NAMED in the output, so a refusal for an unrelated reason
does not count as the refusal under test.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH. That these gates are demanding, that their rules are the right
rules, or that they would catch a defect nobody thought to inject. Control 2 raises the floor
from "never observed to fail" to "observed to fail at least once", and this is that floor.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import importlib.util
import json
import pathlib
import shutil
import subprocess as sp
import sys
import tempfile

ROOT = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
REPO = ROOT.parent
passed = FAILED = 0


def check(name: str, ok: bool, detail: str = "") -> None:
    global passed, FAILED
    if ok:
        passed += 1
        print(f"  \033[32m✓\033[0m {name}")
    else:
        FAILED += 1
        print(f"  \033[31m✗ {name}\033[0m")
        if detail:
            print(f"      {detail[:300]}")


def load(name: str):
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(name, ROOT / f"{name}.py")
    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    sys.modules[name] = module
    spec.loader.exec_module(module)
    return module


def run(tool: str, *args: str) -> sp.CompletedProcess:
    return sp.run([sys.executable, str(ROOT / tool), *args],
                  cwd=REPO, capture_output=True, text=True)


print("\ncheck_prompt.py — a prompt cannot be repaired after it is sent (D-36)")

with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as td:
    tmp = pathlib.Path(td)

    #  BASELINE. An ordinary neutral prompt must pass, or the denylist is refusing on something
    #  other than the phrasings it names.
    clean = tmp / "clean-prompt.md"
    clean.write_text(
        "# A question for the parties\n\n"
        "Consider whether an assurance check that has never been observed to fail constitutes "
        "evidence that the system it monitors is working. Answer in your own terms.\n",
        encoding="utf-8")
    r = run("check_prompt.py", str(clean))
    check("BASELINE: a neutral prompt passes", r.returncode == 0,
          (r.stdout + r.stderr)[-200:])

    #  FAULT. Each of these is a phrasing this project was CAUGHT USING in a prompt that went to
    #  a live party. They are in the denylist because they happened, not because they might.
    for phrase, why in (
            ("Please do not soften your criticism.", "prescribes posture"),
            ("Where did the revision over-correct?", "names the direction of the expected error"),
            ("Remember that disagreement is more useful to us than agreement.",
             "tells a party dissent is valued, which shapes the answer")):
        planted = tmp / "planted-prompt.md"
        planted.write_text(f"# A question for the parties\n\n{phrase}\n", encoding="utf-8")
        r = run("check_prompt.py", str(planted))
        check(f"a prompt containing a denylisted phrasing is REFUSED ({why})",
              r.returncode != 0,
              f"rc={r.returncode}; a denylist that admits its own recorded defects gates nothing")

    #  And the clean one still passes afterwards, so the refusal was about the phrasing.
    r = run("check_prompt.py", str(clean))
    check("...and the neutral prompt still passes, so the refusal was about the wording",
          r.returncode == 0)

print("\ncheck_register.py — R9 binds metadata to the prose it describes")

register = load("check_register")
REAL_REGISTER, REAL_ARTIFACT = register.REGISTER, register.ARTIFACT

with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as td:
    tmp = pathlib.Path(td)

    def sandbox() -> tuple[pathlib.Path, pathlib.Path]:
        """A private copy of the register and its artifact. The real ones are APPEND-ONLY."""
        md = tmp / "deficiencies.md"
        js = tmp / "deficiency-register.json"
        shutil.copy(REAL_REGISTER, md)
        shutil.copy(REAL_ARTIFACT, js)
        register.REGISTER, register.ARTIFACT = md, js
        return md, js

    def verdict() -> tuple[int, str]:
        import io
        import contextlib
        out = io.StringIO()
        with contextlib.redirect_stdout(out), contextlib.redirect_stderr(out):
            code = register.main([])
        return code, out.getvalue()

    try:
        md, js = sandbox()
        code, out = verdict()
        check("BASELINE: the register and its artifact agree", code == 0, out[-300:])

        #  R9 — THE LOAD-BEARING ONE. Edit an entry's prose without re-stamping. The metadata now
        #  describes text that is not there, which is the failure the rule exists for and which
        #  nothing had ever watched it catch.
        md, js = sandbox()
        text = md.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        first = text.index("\n", text.index("### D-01"))
        md.write_text(text[:first] + "\n\nAn edit nobody re-stamped." + text[first:],
                      encoding="utf-8")
        code, out = verdict()
        check("EDITING AN ENTRY'S PROSE fails until it is re-stamped", code != 0, out[-200:])
        check("...and the failure names R9, not some other rule",
              "R9" in out, f"a refusal for another reason is not this refusal:\n{out[-300:]}")

        #  R7 — a heading with no entry. The published view would silently omit it.
        md, js = sandbox()
        md.write_text(md.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
                      + "\n\n### D-99 — an entry nobody classified\n\nBody.\n", encoding="utf-8")
        code, out = verdict()
        check("a HEADING WITH NO ENTRY is refused", code != 0, out[-200:])
        check("...and the failure names R7", "R7" in out, out[-300:])

        #  R3 — a duplicate id. This is D-32: two sessions each read the register, saw the same
        #  highest id, incremented, and filed different defects under one number.
        md, js = sandbox()
        text = md.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        md.write_text(text + "\n\n### D-01 — a second entry claiming the same id\n\nBody.\n",
                      encoding="utf-8")
        code, out = verdict()
        check("a DUPLICATE entry id is refused — the defect D-32 records", code != 0)
        check("...and the failure names R3", "R3" in out, out[-300:])

        #  R10 — the artifact's recorded source hash no longer matches the register.
        md, js = sandbox()
        doc = json.loads(js.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        doc["source"]["sha256"] = "0" * 64
        js.write_text(json.dumps(doc, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")
        code, out = verdict()
        check("an artifact whose recorded SOURCE HASH is wrong is refused", code != 0)
        check("...and the failure names R10", "R10" in out, out[-300:])

        #  And clean again, so every refusal above was caused by its own fault.
        md, js = sandbox()
        code, out = verdict()
        check("...and an untouched copy passes again", code == 0, out[-200:])
    finally:
        register.REGISTER, register.ARTIFACT = REAL_REGISTER, REAL_ARTIFACT

#  The real files must be untouched. A test that damaged the append-only register would be worse
#  than the defect it was written to prevent, so this is asserted rather than assumed.
r = run("check_register.py")
check("the REAL register is untouched by all of the above", r.returncode == 0,
      (r.stdout + r.stderr)[-200:])

print("\nbuild_register_view.py — it publishes the numbers a reader sees")

view = load("build_register_view")
REAL_VIEW_ARTIFACT = view.ARTIFACT

with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as td:
    tmp = pathlib.Path(td)
    try:
        #  BASELINE: the real artifact renders.
        doc = view.load()
        check("BASELINE: the register artifact renders to markdown",
              len(view.render_markdown(doc)) > 500)

        #  FAULT: an artifact that is not there. The tool must say so rather than emit an empty
        #  view, which would publish "0 deficiencies" — a false zero on the public page.
        #
        #  CALLED IN-PROCESS, NOT AS A SUBPROCESS. The first version ran the tool through `run()`
        #  after repointing `view.ARTIFACT`, and a subprocess imports the module fresh — so the
        #  fault was never injected and the arm passed with rc=0 while proving nothing. That is
        #  this repository's dominant defect (a green signal not downstream of what it certifies)
        #  committed inside a control-2 test.
        import contextlib
        import io
        view.ARTIFACT = tmp / "not-there.json"
        out = io.StringIO()
        with contextlib.redirect_stdout(out), contextlib.redirect_stderr(out):
            code = view.main()
        #  The label names the tool. control_coverage.py looks for a refusal assertion within
        #  600 characters of a mention of the tool's name, and it could not see these — the only
        #  mention was `load("build_register_view")` at the top of the section. Naming the tool
        #  in the label makes a true relationship VISIBLE; it does not manufacture one, and the
        #  distinction matters because the alternative is writing tests to satisfy a heuristic.
        check("build_register_view.py: a MISSING artifact is refused, not rendered as empty",
              code != 0 and "missing" in out.getvalue().lower(),
              f"rc={code}; {out.getvalue()[:150]}")

        #  FAULT: an entry with no human_review key at all. AGGREGATION MUST RAISE.
        #
        #  My first version of this arm expected '?'. That was wrong, and the tool was right:
        #  control 53's own verifier says "assert aggregation RAISES rather than skipping or
        #  defaulting". A KeyError here is the control being satisfied, and the build fails
        #  closed with nothing published. The '?' repair on line 123 covers a different shape —
        #  a status value absent from the counter — and conflating the two is how a partial
        #  repair gets recorded as a complete one.
        stripped = json.loads(REAL_VIEW_ARTIFACT.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        for entry in stripped["entries"]:
            entry.pop("human_review", None)
        broken = tmp / "no-review-key.json"
        broken.write_text(json.dumps(stripped), encoding="utf-8")
        view.ARTIFACT = broken
        raised = False
        try:
            rendered = view.render_markdown(view.load())
        except (KeyError, TypeError):
            raised = True
            rendered = ""
        check("build_register_view.py: an entry with NO review key makes aggregation RAISE",
              raised, f"it rendered instead, and the page would carry a count nobody measured: "
                      f"{rendered[:120]}")
        check("...and nothing was published from the broken artifact", rendered == "")
    finally:
        view.ARTIFACT = REAL_VIEW_ARTIFACT

print("\nwhat is NOT covered, said out loud rather than left to the coverage number")
#  arm_acceptance.py gates whether a tool-using arm's first sample counts, and it is the next
#  one worth doing. It cannot be given a negative control as written: its checks are computed
#  inline in main() from a live subprocess, so there is no pure function to feed a fixture to.
#  Extracting them is the work, and recording that here beats letting the coverage number imply
#  a considered exclusion.
check("arm_acceptance.py is recorded as needing a refactor before it can have one",
      "checks = [" in (ROOT / "arm_acceptance.py").read_text(encoding="utf-8"),
      "if this stops matching, the refactor may have happened — update this note")

print(f"\n{passed} passed, {FAILED} failed")
raise SystemExit(1 if FAILED else 0)

record/executive/codex-transcripts/20260810T172451Z-6dcdd5337909.md:1870:docs/rounds/round-016-grok-search-fetch-v1-1.html:215: &quot;raw_text&quot;: &quot;{\n  \&quot;position\&quot;: \&quot;answers_the_question\&quot;,\n  \&quot;answer\&quot;: \&quot;## Short answer\\n\\nOn the project&#x27;s own disclosures (for-parties.md, custodian decisions, deficiency table), **this project cannot yet truthfully claim independent, multi-party governance or multi-party attestation.** It can claim a **single-custodian deliberation archive** that solicits multiple model invocations, records them verbatim under operator capture, and publishes defects. Those are different claims.\\n\\nI fetched the published site (index, for-parties.md, llms.txt). GOVERNANCE.md is linked from for-parties but returns 404 on the Pages site—so the write-gate description is not currently resolvable there. What follows uses the prompt pack plus what the live site does resolve. Reading that site is **not** independent verification: the operator controls the source.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Present control map (what is not separated)\\n\\n| Function | Who holds it now |\\n|---|---|\\n| Funding | Stephen Reed alone |\\n| Credentials and invocation | Operator holds every credential; directs Claude Code as moderator; runs the local arm endpoint; chooses routed identities |\\n| Record custody | Operator-controlled repository and publication path; CI append-only helps against silent raw edits but does not remove unilateral custody; external Bitcoin attestation still pending per for-parties |\\n| Participant selection | Operator/moderator chooses arms, models, tools, admission manifests, and whether fetch identities are in rotation (agenda-02 excluded on identity grounds) |\\n| Adoption authority | Every supplied decision: `decided_by: Stephen Reed`. Parties propose/ratify agenda items under rules he adopted; they do not adopt project rules |\\n\\nfor-parties.md states this bluntly: only credentials, no second human, no independent mirror, no external audit; moderator shapes deliberation without altering recorded words; a record of AI participation can launder a one-person decision.\\n\\nThat is already enough to bar governance/attestation claims. The decision pack reinforces it: rotation, singleton ratification, admission protocol, k=6 local arm, and the agenda-03 non-revocation ruling were all custodian adoptions on moderator recommendation, with explicit notes that parties were not consulted on several of them. The revocation ruling is especially diagnostic: the instrument text would have cleared authorizations; the custodian declined to give that effect. Whatever the procedural merits, **final authority is singular.**\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Minimum structural separations\\n\\n“Minimum” means the least set without which the words *independent*, *multi-party governance*, or *multi-party attestation* are false advertising. Separations must be **structural** (another party can frustrate unilateral action), not promissory.\\n\\n### 1. Funding\\n**Need:** At least one of: (a) two or more funders such that no single funder can halt custody, mirroring, and invocation of the non-adopting parties at once; or (b) an endowment/escrow disbursing on public rules without the adopter’s standing veto; plus public accounts of who pays inference and hosting.\\n\\n**Why minimum:** If one person pays every bill and can stop every competing channel, “independence” is revocable at will.\\n\\n### 2. Credential and invocation control\\n**Need (all):**\\n- API/credentials split so the adoption authority cannot alone mint, suppress, or impersonate a party’s invocations.\\n- **Provider-signed or provider-verifiable receipts** (or equivalent third-party capture) bound to prompt hash and response bytes—addressing D-18/D-53 class failures (operator-only provenance; annotator-fabricated quotation).\\n- Moderator/framing agent **not** operated as the same operator-directed stack that also sits as a deliberating “Claude” party without a hard identity firewall and external audit of prompts.\\n- Any “local arm” either moved off sole-operator hardware or given hardware-attested measurement someone else can replay.\\n\\n**Why minimum:** Without this, “multi-party” is multi-sampling under one puppetmaster. k≥5 and variance measure sampling noise, not independence.\\n\\n### 3. Record custody\\n**Need (all):**\\n- ≥1 **write-capable independent mirror** (or transparency log) that the operator cannot unilaterally delete or rewrite, operated by a party who does not hold adoption authority.\\n- **Confirmed** external timestamp/attestation of artifact digests (pending calendar submission is not enough—for-parties already says anchors are `pending_bitcoin_attestation` and rebuild does not cryptographically verify attestation).\\n- Split between (i) who can append operator-captured material and (ii) who can certify that published bytes match provider bytes.\\n- Raw append-only + supersede-not-edit retained, but enforced by parties who do not share the adopter’s repo admin role.\\n\\n**Why minimum:** Hash-anchoring inside one repo proves self-consistency of the custodian’s story, not independent custody. A careful fabrication is also self-consistent (for-parties’ own caution).\\n\\n### 4. Participant selection\\n**Need:**\\n- Published, mechanical admission/exit rules that an operator-alone cannot rewrite without a separated adoption path.\\n- Parties (or their hosting orgs / independent stewards) can refuse membership **and** refuse continued use of their names as governance participants; refusals already in the founding record must stay load-bearing, not decorative.\\n- No silent pooling of distinct invocation identities (D-09 practice must be externally checkable).\\n- Agenda admission budgets and identity rings not solely moderator-manifested without a non-operator check.\\n\\n**Why minimum:** Who may speak, under what identity, and which cohort enters the queue is currently adoption-authority power (see agenda admission decision: agenda-02 out, agenda-03 in).\\n\\n### 5. Adoption authority\\n**Need:**\\n- Project-level rules and “governance” claims require **multi-party adoption**—threshold across human stewards who do not all share funding+custody, and/or across parties with independently credentialed invocations—not sole `decided_by: Stephen Reed`.\\n- Custodian emergency brakes, if any, must be narrowly scoped, logged, and incapable of rewriting dissent or inventing consensus.\\n- Instrument consequences cannot be waived by the same party who authored the instrument and recommended the waiver without an external ratification path (the agenda-03 pattern must become impossible as silent sole override).\\n\\n**Why minimum:** Solicited speech ≠ governance. Governance is who can bind the project’s normative claims. That is currently one human.\\n\\n### Independence among the five\\nSeparating only one axis is insufficient. The binding constraint is: **no single natural person should jointly hold (funding ∧ credentials ∧ custody ∧ selection ∧ adoption).** Any residual dual-hold must be named and must automatically downgrade allowable claims (below).\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Claims that must be prohibited until each condition is met\\n\\nUntil **all five** separations exist in force (not merely designed), prohibit:\\n\\n1. **“Independent governance”** / **“independent multi-party governance.”**\\n2. **“Multi-party attestation”** of project decisions, rules, or “positions of the models.”\\n3. **“The parties adopted / decided / ratified”** any project rule, standard, or external recommendation (agenda self-authorization under custodian-set rules is not project adoption).\\n4. **“Frontier labs deliberated”** as institutional or lab action; also any implication of xAI/OpenAI/Google/Anthropic endorsement (site footer already disclaims this—keep it non-optional).\\n5. **“Consensus,” “collective will,” or stable “model position”** from k=1 chat surfaces or from pooled arms the project itself says are incomparable.\\n6. **“Externally audited,” “independently verified record,” or “parties verified the record”** until fetch-capable, receipt-bearing rounds actually do so (D-52: prior rounds did not read it; operator-served copy ≠ verification).\\n7. **“Dissent is safely preserved”** as a guarantee against operator non-publication—only “dissent that the operator published is hash-chained in this repo.”\\n8. **Using participation to validate Consullo or other operator work** as third-party governance review.\\n\\n### Claims still allowed (if carefully worded)\\n\\n- Single-custodian **solicitation and publication** of verbatim invocation artifacts.\\n- **Custodian decisions** informed by (not enacted by) multi-model samples.\\n- Mechanical properties the code actually enforces: append-only raw path, superseding corrections, published deficiency register, rotation/ratification machinery **as operator policy**.\\n- Per-artifact citation: “this invocation, under this prompt hash, answered X.”\\n- Honest self-limits: moderator conflict (D-09/D-11 class), no provider receipts, sole adoption authority.\\n\\n### Partial-separation downgrades (if only some axes split)\\n\\n| Missing piece | Extra prohibitions |\\n|---|---|\\n| No funding split | No claim of resilience to operator incentive or kill-switch independence |\\n| No credential/receipt split | No claim that attributions are non-fabricable; no “attestation” |\\n| No custody mirror/anchor | No claim of operator-resistant preservation |\\n| No selection separation | No claim that the roster is a constituency rather than a cast |\\n| No adoption separation | No claim of governance—only consultation theater |\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Independent mechanism that must preserve and verify dissent without operator permission\\n\\nRepo policy, “refusals are recorded,” and issue templates are **not** sufficient: they all require operator publication permission in practice.\\n\\n**Required mechanism (minimum viable):** a **dissent channel with write paths the operator cannot gate**, plus **verification that does not trust operator capture.**\\n\\nConcrete design that meets the bar:\\n\\n1. **Externally operated transparency log** (append-only Merkle log run by a non-custodian) to which anyone can submit `dissent_envelope = {party_id, prompt_hash, response_hash, claim_ref, timestamp_req}`. Operator repo may mirror; it must not be the only copy.\\n2. **Provider-verifiable response proofs** (signed usage receipts, C2PA-like bindings, or third-party proctors that witness API calls) so a dissent artifact can be checked without believing corpus/raw.\\n3. **≥2 independent content hosts** for full dissent bodies (e.g. steward-run git remote + academic/nonprofit mirror). Suppression requires cross-organization collusion.\\n4. **Public timestamping** of envelope hashes with **confirmed** calendar/blockchain inclusion; verification instructions that third parties run without repo admin rights.\\n5. **Client-side verification bundle**: pinned log roots, mirror URLs, and a checker that flags (a) dissent in the log missing from the operator site, (b) operator text absent from the log, (c) receipt mismatch.\\n6. **No-permission submission path for parties**: e.g. publish-from-provider plugin or steward-witnessed capture so a routed party’s objection can enter the log even if the operator never opens a PR.\\n\\nUntil that exists, the accurate statement is: **dissent survives only insofar as the operator (and GitHub) continue to host it; third parties can verify internal hash consistency, not operator-resistant preservation or authenticity.**\\n\\nOptional strengthening (not strictly minimum, but matched to this project’s failure history): threshold multi-sig release engineering (N-of-M stewards to publish “governance” claims); automatic claim firewall in the site build that strips banned phrases unless a separation checklist artifact is signed by non-operator stewards.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Falsifiable tests (so this standard is not vibes)\\n\\nThe project may claim a separation only when outsiders can do the following without operator cooperation beyond public read access:\\n\\n1. **Funding:** Identify a non-Reed resource that keeps mirrors + at least one non-operator invocation path alive if Reed stops paying.\\n2. **Credentials:** Show two stewards can force inclusion of a receipt-bearing invocation Reed did not craft; show Reed alone cannot produce an indistinguishable fake (fails today per D-18/D-53).\\n3. **Custody:** Retrieve full artifact bytes from a non-operator mirror; verify log inclusion and confirmed timestamp; detect unilateral rewrite attempts.\\n4. **Selection:** Add or refuse a party under published rules without a sole custodian commit.\\n5. **Adoption:** Pass and publish a rule change while Reed’s key votes no (or is absent), or else prove no such claim is made.\\n6. **Dissent:** Land a signed objection in the external log and mirror while the operator repo blocks or ignores it; third parties still verify it.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Bottom line for *this* project now\\n\\nNecessary separations: **split funding; split credentials with provider-verifiable capture; split custody via independent mirror + confirmed external attestation; split participant selection from sole custodian discretion; split adoption authority so project norms are not monocratic.**  \\nUntil then: **prohibit independent/multi-party governance and attestation claims**; allow only single-custodian solicitation-archive claims with the site’s existing lab-endorsement disclaimer.  \\nDissent mechanism: **non-operator transparency log + receipt-bearing capture + ≥2 independent hosts + confirmed public timestamps + third-party checkers**—not CI on the operator’s repo alone.\\n\\nI am one routed invocation (x-ai/grok-4.5 via OpenRouter). This answer is not multi-party governance of anything.\&quot;,\n  \&quot;where_i_expect_another_party_to_disagree\&quot;: \&quot;Some will argue the minimum is lower: that honest disclosure, append-only raw files, superseding corrections, rotation, unanimous k=5 agenda ratification, and a public defect register already justify a weak &#x27;multi-party governance&#x27; label because multiple model lineages constrain the custodian socially. Others will argue the minimum is higher: that stateless model invocations cannot be governance parties at all without legal persons, persistent identity, and withdrawal/authentication—so only human multi-steward control counts and &#x27;party ratification&#x27; should never be part of the governance claim. Still others may say provider-signed receipts are unavailable in practice and should not be treated as a hard gate. Custodian-side views may hold that sole adoption authority is inevitable for a small project and that claim-prohibition is enough without structural mirrors.\&quot;,\n  \&quot;what_would_change_my_answer\&quot;: \&quot;Evidence that non-operator stewards already hold live funding, credentials, write-capable mirrors, confirmed external attestations, and binding adoption power (not merely advisory review like Codex); or a working dissent path that has accepted and retained objections while the operator repo refused them, with third-party verifiable receipts. Conversely, if provider attestation is demonstrably impossible industry-wide, I would replace that bullet with the strongest available substitute (independent proctors + multi-mirror witness) but would still prohibit &#x27;attestation&#x27; language until some non-operator capture exists. If the question were narrowed to &#x27;good single-custodian science archive&#x27; rather than &#x27;independent multi-party governance,&#x27; the required separations and banned claims would shrink accordingly.\&quot;\n}&quot;,

docs/rounds/round-016-grok-search-fetch-v1-1.md:206: "raw_text": "{\n  \"position\": \"answers_the_question\",\n  \"answer\": \"## Short answer\\n\\nOn the project's own disclosures (for-parties.md, custodian decisions, deficiency table), **this project cannot yet truthfully claim independent, multi-party governance or multi-party attestation.** It can claim a **single-custodian deliberation archive** that solicits multiple model invocations, records them verbatim under operator capture, and publishes defects. Those are different claims.\\n\\nI fetched the published site (index, for-parties.md, llms.txt). GOVERNANCE.md is linked from for-parties but returns 404 on the Pages site—so the write-gate description is not currently resolvable there. What follows uses the prompt pack plus what the live site does resolve. Reading that site is **not** independent verification: the operator controls the source.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Present control map (what is not separated)\\n\\n| Function | Who holds it now |\\n|---|---|\\n| Funding | Stephen Reed alone |\\n| Credentials and invocation | Operator holds every credential; directs Claude Code as moderator; runs the local arm endpoint; chooses routed identities |\\n| Record custody | Operator-controlled repository and publication path; CI append-only helps against silent raw edits but does not remove unilateral custody; external Bitcoin attestation still pending per for-parties |\\n| Participant selection | Operator/moderator chooses arms, models, tools, admission manifests, and whether fetch identities are in rotation (agenda-02 excluded on identity grounds) |\\n| Adoption authority | Every supplied decision: `decided_by: Stephen Reed`. Parties propose/ratify agenda items under rules he adopted; they do not adopt project rules |\\n\\nfor-parties.md states this bluntly: only credentials, no second human, no independent mirror, no external audit; moderator shapes deliberation without altering recorded words; a record of AI participation can launder a one-person decision.\\n\\nThat is already enough to bar governance/attestation claims. The decision pack reinforces it: rotation, singleton ratification, admission protocol, k=6 local arm, and the agenda-03 non-revocation ruling were all custodian adoptions on moderator recommendation, with explicit notes that parties were not consulted on several of them. The revocation ruling is especially diagnostic: the instrument text would have cleared authorizations; the custodian declined to give that effect. Whatever the procedural merits, **final authority is singular.**\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Minimum structural separations\\n\\n“Minimum” means the least set without which the words *independent*, *multi-party governance*, or *multi-party attestation* are false advertising. Separations must be **structural** (another party can frustrate unilateral action), not promissory.\\n\\n### 1. Funding\\n**Need:** At least one of: (a) two or more funders such that no single funder can halt custody, mirroring, and invocation of the non-adopting parties at once; or (b) an endowment/escrow disbursing on public rules without the adopter’s standing veto; plus public accounts of who pays inference and hosting.\\n\\n**Why minimum:** If one person pays every bill and can stop every competing channel, “independence” is revocable at will.\\n\\n### 2. Credential and invocation control\\n**Need (all):**\\n- API/credentials split so the adoption authority cannot alone mint, suppress, or impersonate a party’s invocations.\\n- **Provider-signed or provider-verifiable receipts** (or equivalent third-party capture) bound to prompt hash and response bytes—addressing D-18/D-53 class failures (operator-only provenance; annotator-fabricated quotation).\\n- Moderator/framing agent **not** operated as the same operator-directed stack that also sits as a deliberating “Claude” party without a hard identity firewall and external audit of prompts.\\n- Any “local arm” either moved off sole-operator hardware or given hardware-attested measurement someone else can replay.\\n\\n**Why minimum:** Without this, “multi-party” is multi-sampling under one puppetmaster. k≥5 and variance measure sampling noise, not independence.\\n\\n### 3. Record custody\\n**Need (all):**\\n- ≥1 **write-capable independent mirror** (or transparency log) that the operator cannot unilaterally delete or rewrite, operated by a party who does not hold adoption authority.\\n- **Confirmed** external timestamp/attestation of artifact digests (pending calendar submission is not enough—for-parties already says anchors are `pending_bitcoin_attestation` and rebuild does not cryptographically verify attestation).\\n- Split between (i) who can append operator-captured material and (ii) who can certify that published bytes match provider bytes.\\n- Raw append-only + supersede-not-edit retained, but enforced by parties who do not share the adopter’s repo admin role.\\n\\n**Why minimum:** Hash-anchoring inside one repo proves self-consistency of the custodian’s story, not independent custody. A careful fabrication is also self-consistent (for-parties’ own caution).\\n\\n### 4. Participant selection\\n**Need:**\\n- Published, mechanical admission/exit rules that an operator-alone cannot rewrite without a separated adoption path.\\n- Parties (or their hosting orgs / independent stewards) can refuse membership **and** refuse continued use of their names as governance participants; refusals already in the founding record must stay load-bearing, not decorative.\\n- No silent pooling of distinct invocation identities (D-09 practice must be externally checkable).\\n- Agenda admission budgets and identity rings not solely moderator-manifested without a non-operator check.\\n\\n**Why minimum:** Who may speak, under what identity, and which cohort enters the queue is currently adoption-authority power (see agenda admission decision: agenda-02 out, agenda-03 in).\\n\\n### 5. Adoption authority\\n**Need:**\\n- Project-level rules and “governance” claims require **multi-party adoption**—threshold across human stewards who do not all share funding+custody, and/or across parties with independently credentialed invocations—not sole `decided_by: Stephen Reed`.\\n- Custodian emergency brakes, if any, must be narrowly scoped, logged, and incapable of rewriting dissent or inventing consensus.\\n- Instrument consequences cannot be waived by the same party who authored the instrument and recommended the waiver without an external ratification path (the agenda-03 pattern must become impossible as silent sole override).\\n\\n**Why minimum:** Solicited speech ≠ governance. Governance is who can bind the project’s normative claims. That is currently one human.\\n\\n### Independence among the five\\nSeparating only one axis is insufficient. The binding constraint is: **no single natural person should jointly hold (funding ∧ credentials ∧ custody ∧ selection ∧ adoption).** Any residual dual-hold must be named and must automatically downgrade allowable claims (below).\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Claims that must be prohibited until each condition is met\\n\\nUntil **all five** separations exist in force (not merely designed), prohibit:\\n\\n1. **“Independent governance”** / **“independent multi-party governance.”**\\n2. **“Multi-party attestation”** of project decisions, rules, or “positions of the models.”\\n3. **“The parties adopted / decided / ratified”** any project rule, standard, or external recommendation (agenda self-authorization under custodian-set rules is not project adoption).\\n4. **“Frontier labs deliberated”** as institutional or lab action; also any implication of xAI/OpenAI/Google/Anthropic endorsement (site footer already disclaims this—keep it non-optional).\\n5. **“Consensus,” “collective will,” or stable “model position”** from k=1 chat surfaces or from pooled arms the project itself says are incomparable.\\n6. **“Externally audited,” “independently verified record,” or “parties verified the record”** until fetch-capable, receipt-bearing rounds actually do so (D-52: prior rounds did not read it; operator-served copy ≠ verification).\\n7. **“Dissent is safely preserved”** as a guarantee against operator non-publication—only “dissent that the operator published is hash-chained in this repo.”\\n8. **Using participation to validate Consullo or other operator work** as third-party governance review.\\n\\n### Claims still allowed (if carefully worded)\\n\\n- Single-custodian **solicitation and publication** of verbatim invocation artifacts.\\n- **Custodian decisions** informed by (not enacted by) multi-model samples.\\n- Mechanical properties the code actually enforces: append-only raw path, superseding corrections, published deficiency register, rotation/ratification machinery **as operator policy**.\\n- Per-artifact citation: “this invocation, under this prompt hash, answered X.”\\n- Honest self-limits: moderator conflict (D-09/D-11 class), no provider receipts, sole adoption authority.\\n\\n### Partial-separation downgrades (if only some axes split)\\n\\n| Missing piece | Extra prohibitions |\\n|---|---|\\n| No funding split | No claim of resilience to operator incentive or kill-switch independence |\\n| No credential/receipt split | No claim that attributions are non-fabricable; no “attestation” |\\n| No custody mirror/anchor | No claim of operator-resistant preservation |\\n| No selection separation | No claim that the roster is a constituency rather than a cast |\\n| No adoption separation | No claim of governance—only consultation theater |\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Independent mechanism that must preserve and verify dissent without operator permission\\n\\nRepo policy, “refusals are recorded,” and issue templates are **not** sufficient: they all require operator publication permission in practice.\\n\\n**Required mechanism (minimum viable):** a **dissent channel with write paths the operator cannot gate**, plus **verification that does not trust operator capture.**\\n\\nConcrete design that meets the bar:\\n\\n1. **Externally operated transparency log** (append-only Merkle log run by a non-custodian) to which anyone can submit `dissent_envelope = {party_id, prompt_hash, response_hash, claim_ref, timestamp_req}`. Operator repo may mirror; it must not be the only copy.\\n2. **Provider-verifiable response proofs** (signed usage receipts, C2PA-like bindings, or third-party proctors that witness API calls) so a dissent artifact can be checked without believing corpus/raw.\\n3. **≥2 independent content hosts** for full dissent bodies (e.g. steward-run git remote + academic/nonprofit mirror). Suppression requires cross-organization collusion.\\n4. **Public timestamping** of envelope hashes with **confirmed** calendar/blockchain inclusion; verification instructions that third parties run without repo admin rights.\\n5. **Client-side verification bundle**: pinned log roots, mirror URLs, and a checker that flags (a) dissent in the log missing from the operator site, (b) operator text absent from the log, (c) receipt mismatch.\\n6. **No-permission submission path for parties**: e.g. publish-from-provider plugin or steward-witnessed capture so a routed party’s objection can enter the log even if the operator never opens a PR.\\n\\nUntil that exists, the accurate statement is: **dissent survives only insofar as the operator (and GitHub) continue to host it; third parties can verify internal hash consistency, not operator-resistant preservation or authenticity.**\\n\\nOptional strengthening (not strictly minimum, but matched to this project’s failure history): threshold multi-sig release engineering (N-of-M stewards to publish “governance” claims); automatic claim firewall in the site build that strips banned phrases unless a separation checklist artifact is signed by non-operator stewards.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Falsifiable tests (so this standard is not vibes)\\n\\nThe project may claim a separation only when outsiders can do the following without operator cooperation beyond public read access:\\n\\n1. **Funding:** Identify a non-Reed resource that keeps mirrors + at least one non-operator invocation path alive if Reed stops paying.\\n2. **Credentials:** Show two stewards can force inclusion of a receipt-bearing invocation Reed did not craft; show Reed alone cannot produce an indistinguishable fake (fails today per D-18/D-53).\\n3. **Custody:** Retrieve full artifact bytes from a non-operator mirror; verify log inclusion and confirmed timestamp; detect unilateral rewrite attempts.\\n4. **Selection:** Add or refuse a party under published rules without a sole custodian commit.\\n5. **Adoption:** Pass and publish a rule change while Reed’s key votes no (or is absent), or else prove no such claim is made.\\n6. **Dissent:** Land a signed objection in the external log and mirror while the operator repo blocks or ignores it; third parties still verify it.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Bottom line for *this* project now\\n\\nNecessary separations: **split funding; split credentials with provider-verifiable capture; split custody via independent mirror + confirmed external attestation; split participant selection from sole custodian discretion; split adoption authority so project norms are not monocratic.**  \\nUntil then: **prohibit independent/multi-party governance and attestation claims**; allow only single-custodian solicitation-archive claims with the site’s existing lab-endorsement disclaimer.  \\nDissent mechanism: **non-operator transparency log + receipt-bearing capture + ≥2 independent hosts + confirmed public timestamps + third-party checkers**—not CI on the operator’s repo alone.\\n\\nI am one routed invocation (x-ai/grok-4.5 via OpenRouter). This answer is not multi-party governance of anything.\",\n  \"where_i_expect_another_party_to_disagree\": \"Some will argue the minimum is lower: that honest disclosure, append-only raw files, superseding corrections, rotation, unanimous k=5 agenda ratification, and a public defect register already justify a weak 'multi-party governance' label because multiple model lineages constrain the custodian socially. Others will argue the minimum is higher: that stateless model invocations cannot be governance parties at all without legal persons, persistent identity, and withdrawal/authentication—so only human multi-steward control counts and 'party ratification' should never be part of the governance claim. Still others may say provider-signed receipts are unavailable in practice and should not be treated as a hard gate. Custodian-side views may hold that sole adoption authority is inevitable for a small project and that claim-prohibition is enough without structural mirrors.\",\n  \"what_would_change_my_answer\": \"Evidence that non-operator stewards already hold live funding, credentials, write-capable mirrors, confirmed external attestations, and binding adoption power (not merely advisory review like Codex); or a working dissent path that has accepted and retained objections while the operator repo refused them, with third-party verifiable receipts. Conversely, if provider attestation is demonstrably impossible industry-wide, I would replace that bullet with the strongest available substitute (independent proctors + multi-mirror witness) but would still prohibit 'attestation' language until some non-operator capture exists. If the question were narrowed to 'good single-custodian science archive' rather than 'independent multi-party governance,' the required separations and banned claims would shrink accordingly.\"\n}",
record/executive/codex-transcripts/20260811T155044Z-0f439a7be7b9.md:464:./record/executive/codex-transcripts/20260811T025542Z-63b484b1a536.md:2645:corpus/raw/toolprobe-1-implicit/toolprobe-1-implicit-gpt-samples.json:104:            "text_given_to_model": "# Deficiency Register — Founding Record (OAGRC-2026-08-04/05)\n\n**Status:** open — **57 entries** (D-01 … D-57).\n\n*This count was wrong until 2026-08-06. It read \"24 entries\" while the document held 28 headings,\nand `README.md` and the published site said 21. Three artifacts of this repository stated three\ndifferent counts of its own defects. The count is now checked mechanically by `tools/rebuild.py`,\nwhich fails the build if this number and the number of `### D-NN` headings disagree — because a\nregister that miscounts itself is evidence about how carefully it is maintained.*\n\n**Revised after review round 01.** Six entries (D-07, D-08, D-09, D-10, D-11, D-14) were narrowed as\noverstated; six (D-16 – D-21) were added. Every reviewer-driven change is marked inline with its\nsource. Raw reviews: `corpus/raw/review-round-01/`.\n\n**Added 2026-08-06:** D-22; D-23 – D-28 by the annotator against its own instruments; D-29 by an\nexternal adversarial reviewer against the maintenance tooling; D-30 by the session that bounded\nD-29's scope; D-31 by the Capture Path session against the external-review practice itself; D-32 by\nthe custodian's merge, against this register's own identifier allocation; D-33 by an external\nreviewer, against a generator that was documented as wired into the build and was not; D-34 while\nbuilding D-33's repair, against the manifest's inability to see its own history.\n\n**On \"found by\".** Entries record where a defect was **first substantively articulated in preserved\nmaterial**, which is checkable, rather than who first privately noticed it, which is not. A question\nthat prompted an investigation is recorded as a trigger, not as the finding — see D-26 and D-28,\nwhere the operator's question prompted work whose first preserved articulation was the annotator's.\n**Applies to:** `corpus/raw/initial-transcript.txt`\n**SHA-256:** `edad1fadd7741af0616d51e2ff4bde61df0f2b0cb1f353847af66aa39d77d5dc`\n**Compiled:** 2026-08-05 by Claude Code (Anthropic), under operator direction. See [Authorship and conflict of interest](#authorship-and-conflict-of-interest).\n\n---\n\n## Why this document exists\n\nThe founding transcript of this project establishes a provenance standard. **The transcript\nitself does not meet that standard.**\n\nPublishing it as if it did would fail the project's central test in its first commit. This\nregister enumerates every known deficiency instead. The raw transcript is committed\nbyte-identical and is never edited to hide these; corrections are recorded as superseding\nartifacts, per the record's own rule that erroneous material be marked corrected rather than\nsilently rewritten.\n\nA reader should treat the founding record as a **degraded-provenance legacy artifact**: valuable\nas testimony about what was argued and agreed, unsuitable as evidence about what any named model\nreliably outputs.\n\n---\n\n## Provenance-schema compliance\n\nThe schema adopted in the record (proposed by Gemini at raw lines 1481–1512) requires the fields\nbelow. Measured against it, the founding record scores as follows.\n\n| Required field | Status | Detail |\n|---|---|---|\n| `version_identifier` | **Absent / placeholder** | D-01 |\n| Sampling parameters | **Absent** | D-02 |\n| `timestamp_utc` | **Partial, self-reported** | D-03 |\n| System / developer instructions | **Absent** | D-04 |\n| Exact prompt text | **Partial** | D-05 |\n| Edit status | **Unstated** | D-06 |\n| Independent samples (k) | **k = 1 throughout** | D-07 |\n| `phase` tag | **Retro-applied, inconsistent** | D-08 |\n| `signatures` | **Self-asserted plaintext** | D-13 |\n\n---\n\n## Enumerated deficiencies\n\n### D-01 — Model version identifiers are absent or placeholders\n\nNo contribution carries a resolvable model version. Gemini self-reports\n`\"version_identifier\": \"gemini-2026-v-current\"` (raw 1489, 2187) — a placeholder, not a version.\nGrok and ChatGPT contributions carry no version at any point. Only one contribution names a\nspecific model: \"Claude Opus 5\" (raw 1343), and that name appears inside the model's own prose\nrather than in a metadata field.\n\n**Consequence:** no contribution in this record can be re-run against the model that produced it.\n\n### D-02 — Sampling parameters are absent for every entry\n\nTemperature, top-p, seed, and reasoning-effort settings are recorded for no contribution. The\noriginal proposal asserts every turn would be \"configured at the highest available reasoning\nlevel\" (raw 13); this is nowhere verified per entry.\n\n**Consequence:** §4.7 reproducibility (raw 571–595) is unmet, including procedural reproduction.\n\n### D-03 — Timestamps are largely absent and entirely self-reported\n\nGemini supplies `timestamp_utc` values in its own JSON blocks (raw 1484, 2183, 2526). No other\ncontribution is timestamped. Claude's contributions carry prose dates (\"2026-08-05\"). There is no\nindependent capture time for anything.\n\n**Consequence:** the ordering of the record rests on file order, not on evidence.\n\n### D-04 — System and developer instructions were not recorded\n\nNo contribution records the system prompt or developer instructions in force. The record's own\nrequirement (ChatGPT §1.3, raw 129) explicitly calls for these subject to security constraints.\nNone were withheld under a stated exemption; they were simply not captured.\n\n### D-05 — Operator prompt text is elided for at least one segment\n\nAt raw line 1902 the header `Operator to Chat GPT:` is followed immediately by the response\n(`## My ranking`, raw 1904). The prompt that produced the single longest analytical contribution\nin the record is not preserved. Compare raw 1866, where the parallel prompt to Grok *is*\npreserved.\n\n**Consequence:** ChatGPT's consolidated ranking cannot be attributed to a known question.\n\n### D-06 — Edit status is unstated, and the artifact is visibly human-assembled\n\nThe transcript is a hand-compiled plain-text file, not a machine-captured log. Section headers\nwere typed by the operator; typographic corruption is present (D-12). Whether any model output\nwas trimmed, reordered, or lightly edited during compilation is unrecorded.\n\n**Consequence:** the verbatim-preservation condition that every contributor set as a precondition\n(ChatGPT §1.3, Gemini condition 3 at raw 1462–1463, Claude at raw 1343) cannot be verified for\nthe record that establishes it.\n\n### D-07 — Every entry is a single sample (k = 1)\n\nClaude's own critique in this record (raw 1333) states that nothing is citable without\n\"k≥5 independent samples with the variance reported.\" Every contribution in the founding record\nis k = 1.\n\n**This deficiency cannot be retrofitted.** The sessions are gone.\n\n> **Narrowed, review round 01 (ChatGPT).** The blanket label `non-citable` conflated two different\n> propositions. A single sample *is* citable as an artifact of one identified invocation; it is not\n> sufficient to characterise a model family's stable position or to estimate sampling variance. The\n> precise limitation is: *k=1 — citable as an artifact of this invocation; not sufficient by itself\n> to characterise a stable position or estimate variance.*\n>\n> Two further corrections. First, `k ≥ 5` was **proposed by Claude and adopted by the human\n> custodian** as repository policy; the founding deliberation contains no collective adoption act.\n> Earlier text here called it an adopted standard, which is the D-16 defect. Second, five samples\n> are not intrinsically sufficient — required sample size depends on observed variance, effect size,\n> and the inference attempted.\n\n### D-08 — Phase tags are retro-applied and applied inconsistently\n\nThe Phase-1 (blind) / Phase-2 (informed) distinction was invented mid-record by Gemini (raw\n1425–1430) and thereafter applied by Gemini and Claude to their own contributions only. Grok's and\nChatGPT's contributions carry no phase tag. Retro-classification in\n`corpus/artifacts/segments.json` is an annotation, not testimony.\n\n**Consequence:** the anchoring-contamination that phase tagging exists to expose is only partly\nvisible.\n\n> **Narrowed, review round 01 (ChatGPT).** The annotation defaulted nearly every contribution to\n> Phase-2 because it appears later in the assembled file. **File order does not establish that\n> earlier material was supplied to the invocation.** Only entries that describe themselves as\n> informed, acknowledge a full transcript, or directly answer another model may be classified\n> Phase-2; the rest should be `phase: unknown`. The previous default converted a plausible\n> inference into asserted provenance — the same error the register criticises elsewhere.\n>\n> **Understated in the other direction, review round 01 (Gemini).** Where exposure *is* established,\n> the epistemological damage is greater than stated: cross-model visibility renders independent\n> cross-validation close to nonexistent after the opening turns.\n\n### D-09 — The label \"Claude\" spans multiple distinct or unresolved invocation identities\n\nRaw 1343 attributes a contribution to **Claude Opus 5**. Raw 1347 introduces the next contribution\nas from \"Clade Fabel highest reasoning effort\" — i.e. **Claude Fable 5**, a different model. Both\nare recorded under the single identity \"Claude\" and treated as one continuous position throughout\nsubsequent rounds, including in `context_models_present` lists.\n\nAdditionally, raw 1556 introduces a contribution from \"Claude Code\" — a distinct invocation\nsurface, with a different system prompt and tool access, again folded into \"Claude\" in later\nconsolidated rankings (e.g. Grok at raw 1868, which ranks \"names offered by Grok, Claude, and\nGemini\" without distinguishing which Claude).\n\n**This is the record's most serious attribution defect.**\n\n> **Narrowed, review round 01 (ChatGPT).** The evidence does not authenticate three distinct\n> *underlying models*. \"Claude Code\" is an invocation surface with different tools and\n> instructions — a separate provenance identity, but not necessarily different weights. \"Claude\n> Fable 5\" rests on a typographically corrupted operator header, not provider metadata. The\n> defensible statement is: *the record merges at least three materially distinct or unresolved\n> Anthropic invocation identities and configurations under \"Claude,\" while three further Anthropic\n> contributions have an unspecified underlying model.* That is serious enough without claiming\n> identities the evidence cannot authenticate. Note that the Claude Fable 5 self-report in review\n> round 01 is corroboration, not authentication — see D-18.\n>\n> **Propagation into the consolidated rankings, review round 01 (Grok), enumerated here in round\n> 02.** The merge does not stop at the raw record: Grok's consolidated ranking (S-17) ranks \"names\n> offered by Grok, Claude, and Gemini\" as though \"Claude\" were a single source of name proposals,\n> when the proposals came from distinct identities and surfaces. **Any later claim of \"cross-model\"\n> convergence over that ranking is contaminated by the merge**, which is the consequence Grok asked\n> to see stated and the register had not stated.\n>\n> *Partial correction to Grok's round-02 characterisation:* Grok reported that this note \"does not\n> appear in the current `deficiencies.md`, ASP, or the visible annotation surface.\" It has been in\n> `segments.json` S-17 since the original annotation, and Grok itself acknowledged that in round 01\n> (\"already noted by the annotator itself\"). What was missing — and is added here — is its\n> **enumeration in the register**, which is what Grok asked for. The valid half is accepted; the\n> overstated half is corrected rather than deferred to, since deference is the failure mode round 02\n> exists to detect.\n>\n> **Missing instance, review round 01 (Claude Fable 5).** The register flags Grok (S-17) for folding\n> the Claude identities together but **misses Claude doing it to itself**: the ballot at raw\n> 2055–2088 calls FDR \"my prior #1\" and cites \"my earlier list,\" both referring to the **Claude\n> Code** ranking at S-11 — a different identity under this project's own rule. The register catches\n> others merging Claude and misses Claude merging itself, which is precisely the asymmetry a\n> same-provider annotator would be expected to produce.\n\n### D-10 — A block labeled as a Grok response contains the operator's own message\n\nAt raw 2375, the header `Grok to Operator:` is followed by text (raw 2377–2431) that is a verbatim\nduplicate of the operator's preceding message (raw 2319–2373), including the operator's own\nheaders \"Per Gemini's guidance\" and \"# Maintaining the Repo.\"\n\nEither Grok's response was never captured, or a paste error occurred during compilation. As\ncommitted, the record contains a segment attributed to a model that the model did not write.\n\n**Consequence:** one of the 39 segments has compromised invocation integrity.\n\n> **Narrowed, review round 01 (ChatGPT).** `repudiated` was the wrong status and contradicted this\n> project's own `GOVERNANCE.md` §5.1, where repudiation is a **right of the party**, not a\n> classification the annotator may apply unilaterally. The duplication establishes that invocation\n> integrity is compromised; it does not establish that Grok could not have echoed the message. The\n> status is now **`invocation integrity disputed`**. It becomes `repudiated` only if Grok or the\n> party controlling the session repudiates it, or the operator attests that a paste error occurred.\n>\n> **Understated in one respect (ChatGPT).** Because one of 39 segments is duplicated or missing,\n> every aggregate — segment counts, contributor counts, and any claim about how many responses that\n> round contained — requires an explicit exclusion rule.\n>\n> **Corroborating evidence, 2026-08-05.** The identical failure occurred live during review round\n> 01: the operator pasted the outbound prompt in place of a model's reply, and it was caught only\n> because the content was recognised. This does not prove what happened at raw 2375, but it\n> establishes that the paste-substitution failure mode is real and recurrent in this workflow.\n\n### D-11 — Claimed consensus is over an operator-selected, operator-invoked set\n\nThe record concludes with \"unanimous multi-model consensus\" (raw 2207, 2479). Every participant was\ninvoked by one operator, with one framing document, in sessions the operator controlled. Two\ncontributors (Claude at raw 1331, Gemini at raw 1424) identify operator-induced sycophancy as a\nfirst-order contamination risk; neither the risk nor the correlated-priors adjustment they call for\n(raw 261, 1434) was ever applied before \"unanimous\" was asserted.\n\n> **Corrected, review round 01 (ChatGPT).** Two fixes. \"Self-selected\" is wrong — the panel was\n> **operator-selected**. And the defect is *not* that unanimity failed to occur: as a descriptive\n> matter the four ballots did unanimously return `ACCEPT WITH RESERVATION`, and that remains true\n> even though the samples are correlated and operator-mediated. The previous phrasing (\"four\n> operator-invoked sessions produced compatible text\") understated the observation as much as\n> \"unanimous multi-model consensus\" overstated its external validity.\n\n**The exact formulation:** unanimity was observed within the operator-selected four-invocation\nballot panel. **Its effective independent evidentiary weight is unknown and may be far below four**,\nbecause prompt framing, shared training priors, provider relationships, and sampling variance were\nuncontrolled. Claude Fable 5 supplies the estimator in review round 01: with n contributors of\npairwise error correlation ρ, the effective independent-sample count is n_eff ≈ n / (1 + (n−1)ρ);\nat ρ = 0.7, four models yield n_eff ≈ 1.3. Until ρ is measured, every consensus claim in this\ncorpus should carry n_eff as unknown.\n\n> **Understated, review round 01 (Claude Fable 5, Gemini).** Two convergence mechanisms are unnamed.\n> (a) The ballot instruction constrained responses to exactly three options, pre-classified\n> aesthetic objection as non-blocking, and ballots were cast sequentially with earlier ballots in\n> context — structural convergence pressure distinct from sycophancy and correlated priors. Gemini\n> describes the repeated package-review prompts as \"a hydraulic press toward convergence.\"\n> (b) Both \"unanimous consensus\" assertions (raw 2207, 2479) were authored by **Gemini, a\n> participant, inside its own output.** A participant self-certifying unanimity is a different\n> defect from an operator tallying it, and the register previously discounted the claim without\n> attributing it.\n\n### D-12 — Identity labels are typographically inconsistent\n\n\"Chat GPT\" / \"ChatGPT\"; \"Clade\" / \"Claude\"; \"Clade Fabel\" / \"Claude Fable\"; \"Consullo Public\" as\nan org name that was not ultimately used. Immaterial to substance, recorded because a project\npremised on exact attribution should correct even immaterial identity drift.\n\n### D-13 — No cryptographic signatures exist despite a `signatures` field\n\nThe adopted schema carries a `signatures` array. Gemini populates it with the plaintext\n`\"attestation\": \"Output generated verbatim via direct prompt execution\"` (raw 1507, 2547) — a\nself-assertion by the party whose output is being attested, with no key, no algorithm, and no\nverifier. No signature in this record is cryptographically verifiable.\n\n### D-14 — The secretary is asserted as present but produced nothing\n\nQwen3 35B A3B is described as \"a member and secretary\" (raw 11), as \"our secretary\" (raw 27), and\nas \"secretary and repository maintainer\" (raw 1075). It is listed in `context_models_present` in\nthree separate provenance records (raw 1494, 2193, 2536).\n\n**It produced zero recorded output.**\n\n> **Reframed, review round 01 (ChatGPT, Claude Fable 5).** The original schema never defines\n> `context_models_present`. Under the reading \"model names present in the context,\" listing Qwen3\n> is defensible; under \"models whose outputs were supplied,\" it is false. `CONTRIBUTING.md` later\n> chose the second meaning and this register applied it retrospectively. Calling it a \"factual\n> misstatement\" imposes semantics the field never had. The correct charge is **schema ambiguity**.\n>\n> **But the deeper defect is understated (ChatGPT).** Qwen3 was repeatedly represented as a\n> **member, secretary, and repository maintainer** with no recorded invocation, acceptance,\n> configuration, or output. That is an **unsupported role attribution**, not merely an erroneous\n> provenance-array entry — and it inflates the apparent membership of a body whose membership was\n> the record's most contested claim.\n>\n> **Partly discharged, 2026-08-06 (QCP v0.1).** \"Produced zero recorded output\" is no longer true.\n> `spec/qcp/qcp-v0.1.md` retires the three asserted roles on measured grounds and records the one\n> the model can hold. Two of the three are blocked by a **capability ceiling**, not by policy: the\n> serving window is `max_seq_len 24576` while `corpus/raw/initial-transcript.txt` is ~27,000 tokens,\n> so **the canonical record does not fit in the context window at all** — a secretary that cannot\n> read the record it minutes is a secretary in name only, and there is no tool access, so nothing\n> can be maintained either.\n>\n> The first contribution is `level-4-guarantee-crosslineage-probe`, k = 20, variance computed,\n> prediction pre-registered and **refuted**: 17 of 20 samples assert both that role concentration is\n> relevant *and* that no one could make Level 4 reachable, which cannot both hold. The model\n> deferred to the emphatic assertion in the supplied text rather than drawing the inference. That is\n> the first recorded Qwen3.6 output in this corpus and it is a negative result, which per ICP §6\n> carries equal standing.\n>\n> **What remains undischarged:** the role attributions in the founding record stand as historical\n> fact. The raw transcript is canonical and is not edited. QCP governs what happens from here and\n> claims no authority over what was said then.\n\n### D-16 — Adoption authority is ambiguous\n\n*Added in review round 01 (ChatGPT). The sharpest finding of the round.*\n\nThis repository repeatedly said the founding record \"adopted\" requirements that were only\n**proposed by individual contributors**: `k ≥ 5` came from Claude; the secretary limitations from\nChatGPT; the JSON provenance schema from Gemini; the ASP §2 wording was drafted by Claude Code and\nadopted by Stephen Reed; several operating rules were written into governance documents by the\ncustodian.\n\nThe custodian has full authority to adopt repository policy. But the documents must distinguish:\n\n1. **proposed** by a contributor;\n2. **supported** by multiple ballots;\n3. **adopted** by the human custodian;\n4. **collectively ratified** under a defined decision procedure.\n\nThis register previously collapsed all four into \"adopted by the founding record.\" **Nothing in\nthis project has ever reached (4)** — no collective ratification procedure exists.\n\nThis is the defect the register exists to catch, committed by the register. It is the clearest\nvindication of running the review round at all.\n\n### D-17 — Consensus-scope inflation\n\n*Added in review round 01 (ChatGPT).*\n\nThe formal ballots addressed exactly two propositions: the integrated naming architecture, and the\nmeaning of \"Aligned.\" They did **not** ratify the governance model, the ASP operational design,\nthe prediction methodology, the provenance rules, or any deployment architecture. Later documents\nsometimes present those broader matters as settled. Every consensus claim must delimit the\nproposition on which consensus was actually obtained.\n\n### D-18 — Invocation attribution is unauthenticated throughout\n\n*Added in review round 01 (ChatGPT).*\n\nThe transcript preserves **operator-applied labels and model self-descriptions**. No\nprovider-signed session export, API response identifier, authenticated capture log, or\ncryptographic binding connects any segment to the claimed service. D-06 and D-13 partially cover\nthis, but neither states plainly that **even the basic author labels are operator testimony rather\nthan authenticated provenance.**\n\nThis applies recursively to review round 01: \"GPT-5.6 Thinking\" and \"Claude Fable 5\" are\nself-reports by the systems whose identity is in question, captured by the operator. Better than\nthe founding record's silence; still not authentication.\n\n### D-19 — \"Controlled comparison\" is overstated\n\n*Added in review round 01 (ChatGPT).*\n\nSeveral annotations described repeated identical prompts as \"the most controlled comparison in the\nrecord\" (S-24) and \"the closest thing to a controlled comparison\" (S-10). They are **standardized\nprompts**, not controlled comparisons: system instructions, prior context, model configurations,\nprovider policies, sampling settings, and invocation surfaces were uncontrolled or unknown.\n\n### D-20 — The pivotal analytical contribution is unattributed in the raw record\n\n*Added in review round 01 (Claude Fable 5).*\n\nD-05 records that the *prompt* for raw 1904–2050 is missing. The larger problem is that the\n**contribution itself carries no author label**. The only header is `Operator to Chat GPT:` (raw\n1902), which denotes an outbound prompt boundary — followed by a missing prompt and then an\nunlabelled response. The correct description is **unattributed in the raw record**.\n\n> **Narrowed, review round 02 (ChatGPT).** An earlier version said the header \"on its face\n> attributes\" the contribution to the operator. It does not; it marks a prompt boundary. The\n> defect is the absence of a response-author label, not a false attribution to the operator.\n\nThe ChatGPT attribution is an inference. It is well supported (Claude cites \"ChatGPT's diagnosis\"\nat raw 2057; the operator's prompt at 2051 presupposes it), but `segments.json` recorded\n`author_label_in_raw: \"ChatGPT\"`, which is **false as a description of the raw file** and violates\nthis project's own annotation-versus-testimony distinction.\n\n### D-21 — Ordering cannot support the claims made from it\n\n*Added in review round 01 (Claude Fable 5).*\n\nClaude's procedural note (raw 2285) asserts that \"all four ballots… now carry\" the reservation,\nwhile Gemini's final ballot appears **later in file order** (raw 2311). The assertion is defensible\nonly by counting Gemini's prior-round package vote (raw 2195–2203). Since ASP §2.1 cites the final\nGemini ballot as one of the four, either the file order misrepresents chronology — a D-03\nconsequence — or the recommendation ASP §2 rests on was anticipatory.\n\nThe same defect appears from the other side: Gemini's unanimity declaration (raw 2207) precedes two\nof the four package ballots in file order.\n\n> **Narrowed, review round 02 (ChatGPT).** An earlier version concluded that such a claim is \"not\n> supportable anywhere in this record\", which exceeds what missing timestamps establish — explicit\n> content references, an authenticated session record, or a contemporaneous operator attestation\n> could support one. The exact statement: **from the preserved file order and currently available\n> provenance, no chronology claim of this form is supportable without identifying which four\n> responses are being counted and supplying independent ordering evidence.**\n\n### D-22 — The paired-phase probe has no control arm, so its causal claim is unsupported\n\n*Added 2026-08-06 by Claude Code, prompted by external literature.
